body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Blog: How I Learned to Write a Formal Email
paras: When I joined an international research team, my first formal email to a colleague in Tokyo taught me more about **cross-cultural communication** than any textbook. I opened with a casual “Hi!” and went straight to my request. The reply was courteous but cool: I had skipped the salutation, the context and the courtesy that a formal message demands.

Since then I follow a simple **model**: a clear subject line; a respectful salutation (“Dear Dr. Tanaka,”); one sentence stating the purpose; a short paragraph that **elaborates** on the details; a polite request with a deadline; and a closing such as “Yours sincerely,”. When a point needs **elaboration**, I add evidence rather than adjectives.

Tone matters most. In some cultures directness signals efficiency; in others it sounds **abrupt**. I now soften my requests (“I would be grateful if you could…”) and **elaborate** on my reasons, which shows respect for the reader’s time.

items.q: The writer’s first email was too formal.
The model includes one sentence stating the purpose.
The colleague in Tokyo was older than the writer.

blocks.body: Em e-mail formal use **I am writing to…**, formas educadas (**would, could**) e frases completas, sem contrações.
**Dear Dr. Tanaka** vai com **Yours sincerely** (nome conhecido) e **Dear Sir or Madam** com **Yours faithfully**.

items.s: I am ___ to enquire about the vacancy. (write)
Could you ___ on the second point? (elaborate)
I would be ___ if you could reply by Friday. (grateful)
After “Dear Dr. Tanaka” we close with “Yours ___”. (sincerely)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.expt: Observe: triagem da caixa de entrada.

body: **I am writing to enquire about…** — Escrevo para saber sobre…
**I would be grateful if you could…** — Eu agradeceria se você pudesse…
**Please find attached…** — Segue em anexo…
**Should you require further information,…** — Caso precise de mais informações,…
**I look forward to hearing from you.** — Aguardo seu retorno.
**Thank you for your prompt reply.** — Obrigado pela resposta rápida.
**With reference to your email of…** — Em referência ao seu e-mail de…
**Please do not hesitate to contact me.** — Não hesite em me contatar.
**Should I start with “Hi”?** — Devo começar com “Hi”?
**Could you check my email to Dr. Tanaka?** — Você pode revisar meu e-mail para o Dr. Tanaka?
**It is clear, but you could elaborate on the deadline.** — Está claro, mas você poderia detalhar o prazo.

items.label: Ênfase intencional
items.note: Ênfase intencional: a palavra mais importante da frase recebe o acento mais forte e a nota mais alta, para marcar contraste ou correção.
words: It was the POLICY, not the person.
We need MORE time, not more money.

prompts.q: Explain why a formal email needs a subject line.
prompts.model: A clear subject line tells the reader why I am writing.
I would be grateful if you could reply by Friday.
I would be happy to elaborate on any point.

blocks.task: Write a formal email of 6–8 sentences asking a university in another country for information about a course.
blocks.model: Subject: Enquiry about the Master’s programme. Dear Dr. Tanaka, I am writing to enquire about your Master’s programme in Education. I have a degree in languages and three years of teaching experience. Could you elaborate on the entry requirements and the deadline? I would also be grateful if you could send me the fee table. Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely, Marina Costa
